Definition: from G746; original or primeval:--(them of) old (time).
BiblicalUsage: The word means of old time, ancient, from the beginning. Jesus says you have heard it said by them of old time, James says Moses of old time is preached in every city, Peter says God spared not the old world, and Paul says if any man is in Christ, old things are passed away.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe old does not mean outdated, and it does not mean safe either. The old world was drowned, the old things pass away in Christ, and the old words of Moses are still preached, because what is ancient can be either judged or kept.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
